info.destination: The page visitors reach when no targeting rule or A/B variant applies. Must be a full http(s) address.
info.domain: The domain the short link lives on. Add your own branded domain under Domains.
info.slug: The part after the domain, e.g. /spring-sale. Letters, numbers, dot, dash and underscore; it must be unique on the domain.
info.title: Your own label for the link. Also used as the page title in link previews and on cloaked pages.
info.folder: Groups related links in the list. Folders don't affect redirects.
info.description: Short summary used in link previews and on cloaked pages.
info.image: Shown when the short link is shared on social media or in messaging apps.
info.tags: Free-form labels for filtering and reporting. Separate with commas, up to 20.
info.iosDestination: iPhone and iPad visitors go here instead of the main destination, e.g. your App Store page or a universal link. Targeting rules and A/B tests still take priority.
info.androidDestination: Android visitors go here instead of the main destination, e.g. your Google Play page or an app link. Targeting rules and A/B tests still take priority.
info.openMode: Automatic: a normal redirect. Open in the app: on phones, links to YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X, Facebook, Spotify, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram or Pinterest try the app first. Leave in-app browsers: visitors inside Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and similar apps are offered the link in their real browser. Desktop visitors always get a normal redirect.
info.variant: One destination in the split. Visitors are assigned by weight and keep seeing the same variant.
info.weight: Relative share of traffic, 0–100. Weights of 70 and 30 send roughly 70% and 30% of visitors.
info.utmSource: Where the traffic comes from, e.g. newsletter or instagram. Added to the destination as utm_source.
info.utmMedium: The marketing channel, e.g. email, social or cpc.
info.utmTerm: The paid search keyword, if there is one.
info.utmContent: Tells links within one campaign apart, e.g. header-button and footer-link.
info.forwardQuery: Extra parameters on the short link, e.g. ?ref=partner, are copied to the destination. Parameters the destination already has are kept.
info.startsAt: The link goes live at this moment, in your local time. Until then visitors get the domain's not-found page and no clicks are counted.
info.expiresAt: After this moment the link stops sending visitors to the destination. In your local time.
info.expiredDestination: Where visitors go once the link has expired. Leave empty to treat the link as not found.
info.password: Visitors must enter this password before they are redirected. At least 8 characters.
info.cloak: Shows the destination inside a frame so the short URL stays in the address bar. Some sites refuse to be framed, and phones skip cloaking when an open mode applies.
info.noIndex: Asks search engines not to index or follow the short link. Recommended for most links.
info.archive: Archived links stop redirecting but keep their stats. You can unarchive them any time.
info.notes: Private notes for your team. Never shown to visitors.
info.when: What to check about the visitor: location, device, operating system, browser, language, where they came from, or the time.
info.operator: “Is one of” matches any listed value; “is not one of” matches everyone else, including visitors whose value is unknown.
info.referrerOperator: “Contains” looks for the text anywhere in the referring URL, “equals host” compares the referring domain exactly, and “is empty” matches visits without a referrer, such as typed URLs and many apps.
info.countries: Two-letter country codes, detected from the visitor's IP address. Separate with commas.
info.continents: Continent codes, detected from the visitor's IP address: EU Europe, NA North America, SA South America, AS Asia, AF Africa, OC Oceania, AN Antarctica.
info.regions: State or province names exactly as Cloudflare reports them, e.g. Istanbul or California.
info.languages: Matches the language ranked highest in the visitor's browser settings. Regional variants count as the main language, so British English matches English.
info.devices: Phone, tablet or desktop, detected from the browser's user agent.
info.operatingSystems: Detected from the user agent. iPads that request the desktop version of sites may show up as macOS.
info.browsers: Detected from the user agent. Pick browsers here and in-app browsers below; a visitor matches if either applies.
info.inAppBrowsers: Browsers built into social apps. They also match their engine above: Instagram on Android counts as Chrome too.
info.referrerValue: A domain such as google.com, or any part of the referring URL.
info.from: Start of the daily window, in the time zone next to it. If it is later than the end, the window runs past midnight.
info.to: End of the daily window, inclusive.
info.timezone: The IANA time zone the window is read in, e.g. Europe/Istanbul. The visitor's own time zone doesn't matter.
info.days: Weekdays the window applies to, in the chosen time zone.
info.priority: Lower numbers are checked first. The first rule whose conditions all match decides the destination.
info.sendTo: Where visitors matching every condition of this rule are sent.

bio.bgImageInfo: Covers the whole page behind your content and is cropped to fit the screen. Pick a calm image so text stays readable.
bio.buttonColorInfo: Fill and border colour of link buttons. Leave empty to use the theme's colour.
bio.buttonTextColorInfo: Colour of the text on link buttons. Make sure it contrasts with the button colour; empty uses the theme.
bio.textColorInfo: Colour of your name, bio and text blocks. Leave empty to use the theme's colour.
bio.customCssInfo: CSS declarations applied to the page itself, e.g. font-size: 17px; letter-spacing: .02em; border-radius: 24px. Selectors, @ rules and unsupported properties are dropped silently.
bio.adsEnabledInfo: Shows your own promo images around the page — your campaigns, not third-party ads. Turn it off to hide them without deleting the images.
bio.adMobileInfo: Shown above your profile on phones and tablets, hidden on wide screens. A wide landscape image works best.
bio.adLeftInfo: Pinned to the left edge on desktop screens only, about 176 px wide. Use a tall portrait image. Not shown in the live preview.

bio.publishedInfo: Switches the page on or off for visitors. On a saved page it applies instantly without pressing Save, and switching it on clears any schedule.
bio.publishAtInfo: Keeps the page hidden until this moment even while Published is on, then it goes live by itself. Switch Published on first, then pick the date and save.

bio.removePasswordInfo: Removes the password gate when you save, so anyone with the link can open the page again.
bio.seoTitleInfo: Title shown in search results, the browser tab and link previews on social apps. Up to 120 characters; empty uses the display name.
bio.seoDescriptionInfo: Summary under the title in search results and share previews. Up to 300 characters; empty uses your bio.
bio.ogImageInfo: Picture shown when the page link is shared on WhatsApp, X, LinkedIn and similar apps. 1200×630 px works best; empty uses the avatar.
bio.labelInfo: Text on the button, up to 120 characters. Short, action-led labels such as "Shop the collection" get more taps.
bio.destinationInfo: The web address the button opens, e.g. https://acme.com/shop. If you leave out https://, it is added for you.
bio.iconInfo: Optional small square image before the label, such as a product thumbnail. It takes priority over the built-in icon.
bio.emphasisInfo: Highlighted adds a lifted shadow so this button stands out. Use it for one or two key links only.
bio.iconNameInfo: Built-in icon shown before the label when no image is uploaded — e.g. a cart for a shop link.
bio.newTabInfo: New tab keeps your bio page open behind the destination; same tab replaces it. New tab is the usual choice for external sites.
bio.platformInfo: Sets the icon shown in the row. Email opens the visitor's mail app; WhatsApp also accepts a phone number.
bio.urlOrHandleInfo: Paste a profile link or just the username (e.g. acme or @acme) — usernames are turned into the right profile link for the platform. For Email enter the address; for WhatsApp a number with country code.
bio.bodyInfo: Free text up to 2,000 characters. Line breaks are kept; links and formatting are not supported.
bio.alignmentInfo: Centre suits short statements; left is easier to read for longer paragraphs.
bio.headingInfo: A section title that splits your page into groups, e.g. "Latest videos". Up to 120 characters.
bio.imageInfo: Shown at full block width. Any aspect ratio works; landscape images need less scrolling on phones.
bio.altTextInfo: Read aloud by screen readers and shown if the image can't load. Describe what the image shows rather than writing "image of".
bio.linksToInfo: Makes the image clickable, e.g. a campaign banner that opens a landing page. https:// is added if you leave it out.
bio.providerInfo: The service the player comes from. It must match the link you paste next to it.
bio.shareUrlInfo: The normal page link, e.g. youtube.com/watch?v=… or open.spotify.com/track/…. It is turned into an embedded player automatically.
bio.formModeInfo: Email capture saves addresses under Leads, where you can export them as CSV. WhatsApp opens a chat with your number, pre-filled with the visitor's message; nothing is stored.
bio.formButtonInfo: Text on the submit button, up to 40 characters, e.g. "Subscribe" or "Message us".
bio.formTitleInfo: A line above the form telling visitors what they get, e.g. "Get our monthly newsletter".
bio.formWhatsappInfo: Your WhatsApp number in international format with country code, e.g. +905551112233. The chat opens with this number.
bio.formSuccessInfo: Message shown after a visitor submits their email, up to 200 characters. Leave empty for a default thank-you.

qr.title: QR codes
qr.designDesc: The code encodes the short link, so you can change where it goes without reprinting.
qr.emptyDesc: Design a code once, print it, and re-target it later by editing the short link behind it.
qr.heroDesc: Every code encodes a short link, so a printed poster can be pointed somewhere new without reprinting.
qr.needLinkDesc: A QR code always points at one of your short links, so the printed code can be re-targeted later.
qr.encodes: Encodes {url} — edit that link to re-target every printed copy.
qr.payloadTooLongHint: Shorten the caption or pick a shorter link.
qr.encodesHint: The code encodes the short link, so editing the link destination re-targets every printed copy.
qr.svgVector: Vector — scales to any print size.
qr.exportHint: Exports render server-side from the saved style, so the logo is embedded in the file. Unsaved edits are not included.
qr.exportLocked: Create the code to unlock PNG, SVG and PDF exports — they render server-side from the saved style.
qr.targetDesc: What the code points at, and how you will recognise it later.
qr.name: Name
qr.shortLinkHint: Change the link destination later and every printed code follows.
qr.caption: Caption
qr.colourDesc: Scanners read brightness, not hue — keep the modules much darker than the background.
qr.tintFindersHint: Colours the three corner markers separately from the modules.
qr.shapeDesc: Module style, quiet zone and how much damage the code can survive.
qr.errorLocked: Locked to H while a logo covers the centre.
qr.errorHint: Higher levels survive scuffs, folds and reprints.
qr.logoDesc: Centred overlay on a padded backing plate.
qr.logoPaid: Custom logos are available on paid plans. Every other control stays editable.
qr.logoUrlHint: PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG up to 1 MB.
qr.logoHint: Uploaded logos are inlined in both preview and download.
qr.logoKeepSmall: Keep the logo under a quarter of the width — anything larger eats the data the scanner needs.
qr.deleteHint: Printed copies stop resolving to this record. The short link behind it and all of its click history are left untouched.
qr.deleteBullet1: Anything already printed keeps pointing at the short link, not this design.
qr.deleteBullet2: The short link and its click history are not affected.
qr.templatesEmpty: Save your current colours, shape and logo as a template to reuse on the next code.
qr.saveTemplateDesc: Stores colours, module shape, quiet zone, logo and caption — not the link or URL payload.
qr.qualityFailAdvice: Foreground and background are too close in brightness. Darken one of them.
qr.qualityLowAdvice: Readable up close, but likely to fail on a poster or in dim light.
qr.qualityInvertedAdvice: Light modules on a dark background — some older scanners refuse these.
qr.filteredEmptyTitle: No QR codes for this link
qr.filteredEmptyDesc: Design one now — it will encode this short link, so you can re-target it later without reprinting.

linkCard.emptyDesc: Create a printable code for this link in one click. You can restyle it in the designer at any time.
linkCard.moreCodes: {count, plural, one {# code points} other {# codes point}} at this link.

info.name: Only your team sees this name. It labels the code in your QR list and in downloads, and is not encoded in the code.
info.payloadKind: Short link codes are dynamic: change the destination later and every printed copy follows, with scans counted. The other types write their content straight into the code and cannot change after printing.
info.shortLink: The code opens this short link. Scans show up in the link's statistics as QR scans.
info.payloadUrl: Written into the code as-is, so it cannot be re-targeted or tracked. Use a short link if you might need to change it later.
info.vcardName: Full name saved to the phone's contacts when the code is scanned.
info.vcardOrg: Company or organisation shown under the name. Optional.
info.vcardPhone: Include the country code, e.g. +44 20 7946 0000, so the number also works from abroad.
info.vcardEmail: Email address added to the contact card. Optional.
info.vcardUrl: Website added to the contact card — your site or a profile page. Optional.
info.wifiSsid: The network name exactly as devices show it. It is case-sensitive.
info.wifiPassword: Anyone who scans the code can read this password. Leave it empty for open networks.
info.wifiSecurity: Match your router's setting. Most networks use WPA/WPA2; pick Open only for networks without a password.
info.wifiHidden: Turn on if the network does not broadcast its name, so phones know to look for it.
info.caption: Short text printed under the code, such as a call to action. It is part of the image, not of the encoded data.
info.templates: Reusable styles for this workspace: colours, shape, quiet zone, logo and caption. Applying one never changes what the code points at.
info.palettes: Colour pairs with enough contrast to scan reliably — a safe starting point.
info.foreground: Colour of the modules (the dots). Keep it much darker than the background so the code scans reliably.
info.background: Colour behind the modules and around the code. Light colours scan best.
info.tintFinders: Gives the three large corner squares their own colour. Keep it dark: scanners use these squares to find the code.
info.cornerColour: Colour of the three corner squares. It needs the same strong contrast with the background as the foreground.
info.moduleShape: Look of the small modules. Every shape scans; square is the most robust on low-quality prints.
info.errorCorrection: How much of the code can be scratched or covered and still scan. Higher levels make the pattern denser.
info.quietZone: Blank border around the code, in modules. Scanners need at least 2; use 4 for print.
info.exportSize: Default width in pixels for PNG and PDF downloads. SVG is vector and scales to any size.
info.logo: Put your own image, a brand icon or an emoji in the centre. Error correction switches to H so the code still scans.
info.logoSize: Logo width as a share of the code. A larger logo hides more data; stay under 25% for reliable scans.
info.pngSize: Width in pixels of the PNG download. Use 1024 px or more for print.
info.templateName: A name to recognise this style in the template list. Only your workspace sees it.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.description: From a blank workspace to a live short link you can share.

account.title: Create your workspace
account.body: Sign up with email or Google. Personal workspaces start on the free plan; upgrade anytime from Billing when you need custom domains or API access.

domain.title: Choose where links live
domain.body: Every link belongs to a domain. Use the platform domain out of the box, or add your own under Domains once your plan includes custom hostnames.

link.title: Create a link
link.body: Open Links → New link, paste the long URL, pick the domain and optionally set a custom slug. Advanced options — password, expiry, routing rules — can be added now or later.

share.title: Share and measure
share.body: Copy the short URL or download a QR code. Clicks appear on the Dashboard within seconds; open a link’s Stats tab for full breakdowns.

tip.title: Team workspaces
tip.body: Upgrade to a paid plan to create a team workspace. Members share links and domains but keep separate sign-ins; owners and admins manage billing and API keys.

links.title: Links
links.description: Short URLs are the core of Short.ky. This guide covers creation, options and day-to-day management.
links.createBody: Each link maps a slug on a domain to a destination URL. The edge worker resolves the hostname + slug, applies routing rules, then redirects or shows an interstitial.

createSteps.0: Go to Links and click New link.
createSteps.1: Select the domain the slug should live on.
createSteps.2: Enter the destination URL — we normalise schemes and reject unsafe targets.
createSteps.3: Save. The short URL is ready to copy immediately.

links.optionsBody: Open any link from the table to edit these fields. Changes propagate to the edge within seconds.

slug.label: Custom slug
slug.desc: Replace the random code with a readable path like /launch.

password.label: Password
password.desc: Visitors must enter a password before the redirect runs.

expiry.label: Expiry
expiry.desc: Stop redirecting after a date; optionally send expired traffic elsewhere.

utm.label: UTM parameters
utm.desc: Append campaign tags to the destination on redirect.

tags.label: Tags
tags.desc: Label links for filtering in the list and API.

cloak.label: Cloaking
cloak.desc: Show a preview page instead of an instant redirect — useful for social platforms.

links.organizeBody: Use folders to group campaign links. Archive links you no longer promote — they stop accepting clicks but stay in analytics history.
links.relatedRouting: Smart routing — country, device and A/B rules

qrCodes.title: QR codes
qrCodes.description: Turn any link or payload into a downloadable, brand-styled QR code.
qrCodes.createBody: QR codes can point at a Short link (so you can change the destination later) or encode a raw URL, contact card or Wi‑Fi network.

createSteps.0: Open QR codes → New QR code.
createSteps.1: Choose the payload type and fill in the fields.
createSteps.2: Adjust colours, dot style and optional logo, then save.

qrCodes.payloadBody: Link-backed codes inherit routing and analytics from the underlying short link.

rows.linkDesc: Trackable codes tied to an existing short link.
rows.urlDesc: One-off codes that encode a fixed URL.
rows.vcardDesc: Share name, phone and email when scanned.
rows.wifiDesc: Let guests join a network from a poster or menu.

qrCodes.designBody: The designer warns when contrast is too low for reliable scanning.

designTips.0: Keep a quiet zone (margin) around the code — do not crop it flush to artwork.
designTips.1: Prefer dark modules on a light background for maximum compatibility.
designTips.2: Test on paper at the size you plan to print, not just on screen.

bioPages.title: Bio pages
bioPages.description: A hosted link-in-bio page on your domain or a Short.ky handle.
bioPages.handleBody: Each bio page has a unique handle that becomes either yourdomain.com/@handle or handle.short.ky, depending on domain settings.
bioPages.blocksBody: Stack blocks to build the page. Drag to reorder; toggle visibility without deleting content.

blocks.0: Links — buttons to any URL, including other Short links.
blocks.1: Social icons — quick access to profiles.
blocks.2: Text and headings — short bios or announcements.
blocks.4: Lead form — collect email with optional consent text.

bioPages.publishBody: Draft changes stay private until you publish. The public page is cached at the edge for fast loads worldwide.
bioPages.leadsBody: When a lead form block is enabled, submissions appear under Bio → Leads. Export or connect via webhooks on eligible plans.
bioPages.statsBody: Bio views are counted separately from link clicks. Open Stats on a bio page to see views over time and top outbound links.

domains.title: Custom domains
domains.description: Serve short links from your own hostname with automatic TLS.

add.title: Add the hostname
add.body: Under Domains → New domain, enter a dedicated subdomain such as go.acme.com — avoid www.

dns.title: Point DNS
dns.body: Create the CNAME record shown in the panel. If you use Cloudflare, connect the integration to verify in one click.

verify.title: Verify and provision TLS
verify.body: Once DNS propagates, status moves to verified and a certificate is issued automatically.

default.title: Set as default
default.body: Mark one domain as default so new links pre-select it in the editor.

domains.rootBody: Optionally send visitors who hit the domain root to a marketing page, and send unknown slugs to a custom 404 destination.
domains.sslBody: Certificates renew automatically. Keep DNS pointed at Short.ky — removing the CNAME will pause issuance and eventually break HTTPS.

routing.title: Smart routing
routing.description: One short link can send each visitor to a different destination based on context.
routing.howBody: Rules are evaluated at the edge before redirect. The first matching rule wins; if none match, the main destination is used.

rows.abEx: Split 50/50 between two URLs for experiments

routing.priorityBody: Drag rules in the link editor to reorder them. Put the most specific rules first — e.g. country before a broad device rule.
routing.exampleBody: When creating a link via the REST API, include a rules array alongside destination:
routing.mobileBody: Use iosDestination and androidDestination for simple store routing without writing rules. Device-specific rules override these when both are set.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.description: Understand who clicked, from where and on what device.
analytics.dashboardBody: The dashboard aggregates clicks and unique visitors across all links for the selected time range. Top links and recent activity help spot spikes quickly.
analytics.linkBody: Every link has a Stats tab with the same breakdowns scoped to that slug. QR scans and bio views are reported separately.

rows.clicksDesc: Total redirect events, including repeat visits.
rows.visitorsDesc: Unique browsers in the range, deduplicated per link.
rows.referrerDesc: Site or app that sent the visitor.
rows.countryDesc: Geo derived from IP — approximate, not PII.

analytics.rangesBody: Switch between 24 hours and 12 months. Comparisons show the previous period so you can spot trends, not just totals.
analytics.exportBody: On eligible plans, export raw events from Analytics for your own BI tools. API consumers can also pull aggregated stats from GET /links/{id}/stats.

api.title: REST API
api.description: Programmatic access to links, QR codes, bio pages, domains and analytics.
api.authBody: Every request must include a workspace API key. Keys are created in Settings → API and shown in full exactly once.

authTable.scopeValue: One workspace — the key inherits plan limits and quotas.

api.keysBody: Create named keys per environment. Revoke immediately if a key leaks — there is no undo.
api.baseBody: All paths below are relative to:
api.exampleBody: POST /links with domainId and destination. Omit slug to auto-generate one.
api.errorsBody: Errors return JSON with a stable code and human-readable message. Validation errors include field-level details.

rows.plan: Feature not included in current plan (e.g. API on Free).
rows.rate: Hourly limit exceeded — check x-ratelimit-* headers.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.description: Push link and bio events to your backend the moment they happen.
webhooks.setupBody: Register an HTTPS URL and choose which events to receive. Each endpoint gets its own signing secret.
webhooks.settingsBody: Manage endpoints, pause delivery and rotate secrets from Settings → Webhooks.
webhooks.eventsBody: Payloads are JSON POST requests. The event name is included in the body alongside the resource snapshot.

rows.link.created: A link is created via panel or API.
rows.link.clicked: Someone completes a redirect (sampled on high volume).
rows.biopage.viewed: A public bio page is viewed.

webhooks.signatureBody: Each delivery carries x-short-signature: t=timestamp,v1=signature. Compute HMAC-SHA256 with your signing secret over the timestamp, a dot and the raw request body (t.body), then compare the hex digest with v1 in constant time. Reject mismatches and timestamps older than a few minutes.
webhooks.deliveryBody: Your endpoint should respond with 2xx within a few seconds.

deliveryTips.0: Return 200 quickly and process asynchronously if needed.
deliveryTips.1: Disable endpoints you are not using — paused endpoints stop retries.
deliveryTips.2: Store the signing secret in a vault; it cannot be read again from the panel.
